newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Solution for Brazil Bamerindus seen imminent - paper.
newsitem.headline: Solution for Brazil Bamerindus seen imminent - paper.

text.p: The owners of ailing Brazilian private bank Bamerindus expect the central bank to formalize a deal aimed at cleaning up the bank's balance sheets by December 31, a local newspaper said.
Under the terms of a draft of the deal, Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira, Bamerindus' majority shareholder, agrees to give up control of the bank, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said.
Under the plan being negotiated between Bamerindus and the central bank, a group of executives or one private administrator would take over the bank and manage it for a certain period of time.
This group or administrator would hire a private consultant who would help clean up Bamerindus' balance sheets and ready it for an eventual sale to investors later.
For many months, Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank, has been plagued by market speculation that it would be sold due to its liquidity troubles.
Newspapers have reported that private banks Banco Icatu, Pactual and Graphus were the most likely candidates for signing a contract to advise on the bank's management.
